themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 146 this week—a 478% increase from the 25.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 21.04)—suggesting a sudden, widespread deterioration in road quality across Woodhaven/Richmond Hill that demands immediate investigation into root cause and scope.
evidence: 146 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 25.2 weekly average (478% spike, z-score: 21.04)
Concurrent spike in street light condition complaints (13 this week vs. 6.0 average, +117%)
281 active DOB permits filed in last 90 days, including 213 alterations and 7 full demolitions, suggesting ongoing construction/disruption
reporting_angles: Did a single major construction project, utility work, or weather event trigger this spike? Interview DOE, DOT, and utility companies.
Are pothole repairs and street resurfacing backlogs contributing? Request maintenance schedules from NYC Street Maintenance.

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal System Failure
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal condition complaints jumped to 166 last week—a 695% surge from the 20.9 weekly average (z-score: 9.48)—indicating potential citywide or district-specific signal failures that could create safety and congestion hazards.
evidence: 166 traffic signal complaints last week vs. 20.9 weekly average (695% spike, z-score: 9.48)
Spike occurred last week; timing suggests either a discrete failure event or accelerating degradation of signal infrastructure
No overlapping Reddit or news coverage yet, indicating potential under-reported crisis
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DOT to identify which signals failed and whether this is a localized outage or network issue affecting multiple districts.
Interview residents and business owners about traffic congestion, pedestrian safety incidents, and accident reports tied to malfunctioning signals.

themes_detail.label: Noise Surge in Streets & Sidewalks
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 23 this week—a 241% increase from the 6.8 weekly average (z-score: 6.17)—suggesting new or intensified street-level disruption (construction, vendors, or vehicles) that is escalating resident complaints.
evidence: 23 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.8 weekly average (241% spike, z-score: 6.17)

Concurrent spike in street sweeping complaints (3 last week vs. 0.1 average, +2300%) and cannabis retailer complaints (9 last week vs. 1.0 average, +800%), suggesting overlapping street-level commercial and service activity
Residential noise complaints remain elevated at 879 over 90 days, indicating baseline noise burden
reporting_angles: Map this week's street noise complaints to identify geographic hotspots—are they clustered near new cannabis retailers, construction sites, or active street vendors?
Interview residents in high-complaint areas about timing, source, and duration of noise disturbances.

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retail Enforcement Vacuum
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints spiked to 9 last week—an 800% increase from the 1.0 weekly average (z-score: 8.0)—and vendor enforcement complaints rose 1100% from 3 weeks ago, suggesting unregulated or newly opened dispensaries are creating neighborhood friction without adequate city oversight.
evidence: 9 cannabis retailer complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average (800% spike, z-score: 8.0)
3 vendor enforcement complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35), suggesting overlapping street-level commerce issues
Concurrent surge in street noise complaints (241% spike) points to operational disruption from new retailers or enforcement gaps
reporting_angles: Identify which cannabis retailers opened recently in Woodhaven/Richmond Hill and whether they have proper licensing and community board approval.
Interview residents and local business owners about complaints: illegal loitering, odor, foot traffic, or unlicensed operations?

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage & Park Infrastructure
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints spiked to 22 two weeks ago—a 363% increase from the 4.8 weekly average (z-score: 5.94)—coinciding with community board's repeated budget requests for park safety and amenities, suggesting weather damage or maintenance backlog affecting green space quality.
evidence: 22 damaged tree complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 4.8 weekly average (363% spike, z-score: 5.94)

Community board has filed repeated budget requests for 'park safety through more security staff' and 'park or amenity improvements,' indicating sustained concern about park infrastructure and maintenance
Timing (2 weeks ago) suggests possible weather event (high winds, storms) or reactive reporting following severe damage
reporting_angles: Check National Weather Service data for storms or severe weather 2–3 weeks ago that might explain tree damage spike.
Interview Parks Dept. about tree maintenance backlog, inspection schedules, and whether current staffing is adequate for Woodhaven/Richmond Hill parks.
